RBNZ’s Breman: more hikes likely at coming meetings, possibly into restrictive territory
articles.expand: Breman’s guidance partly reverses the dovish read of the hold . Signalling likely hikes at coming meetings, possibly into restrictive territory, should push December pricing back up, support front-end yields and help the New Zealand dollar recover some of its losses. Her explicit worry about a weak currency feeding imported inflation acts as a soft floor for the kiwi, since further falls make a hike more likely. RBA’s Bullock: Inflation is far too high
articles.expand: By saying it is hard to completely look through supply shocks, Bullock signalled that the RBA is less willing to ignore the energy-driven jump in prices than the RBNZ was earlier . Any further rise in crude therefore adds directly to the case for an RBA hike. Her blunt language (more here earlier ), together with firmer core inflation and her view that demand still exceeds supply, supports pricing for a move on November 2 and 3, and backs the Australian dollar and front-end yields. The contrast with the RBNZ’s hold sharpens the policy divergence, which favours AUD/NZD . Bullock’s refusal to gi...

With a hike close to fully priced, the hold is likely to hit the New Zealand dollar and pull front-end yields lower. The 4-3 split and the guidance that tighter policy is still likely should limit how far December pricing unwinds. Policy divergence is now sharp. If the Fed sounds less aggressive than markets fear this week, two-year yields have the most room to fall, which would steepen the curve. Neutral positioning on US equities, with a continued tilt to AI and tech, suggests BlackRock expects volatility around policy, not a broad selloff. A dovish-leaning Fed would also cap the dollar. Steady services inflation strengthens the case for the Outlook Report to effectively declare underlying inflation has reached 2%, which would support the yen and short-end JGB yields. The bigger moves are still likely to come from the BoJ’s vote split, Ueda’s press conference and Wednesday’s Fed decision.
